# Your Discharge Letter

**From the Neurology Team | Admitted: 19 May | Discharged: 20 May**

---

## What Happened

You were brought to hospital after having a seizure (a generalised tonic-clonic seizure) at work. A seizure is when the brain sends out sudden bursts of electrical signals, causing the body to shake and the person to lose consciousness. Yours lasted about 2 minutes. After it stopped, you were confused for a short time, which is normal after this type of seizure. You also had a small bite on the side of your tongue.

This appears to have been a first seizure with no clear cause found so far.

---

## Tests You Had in Hospital

You had blood tests, a blood sugar check, and a drug screen — all of these came back normal. You also had a CT scan of your head, which was normal too.

Two more tests still need to be done as an outpatient (meaning you do not need to stay in hospital for them):

- An **MRI scan of your brain**
- An **EEG** (a test that measures the electrical activity in your brain)

You will be told the dates for these.

---

## Treatment

The doctors did not start any seizure medicines (antiepileptics) at this stage. This is because it was a first seizure and the team felt it was right to wait until your outpatient tests have been done and reviewed before making any decisions about medication.

---

## Medicines to Take at Home

You were not taking any medicines before you came in, and you have not been given any new medicines to take home.

---

## What Happens Next

You have three outpatient appointments being arranged:

1. **MRI brain scan** — date to be confirmed
2. **EEG** — date to be confirmed
3. **First-fit clinic** (a specialist neurology outpatient appointment) — date to be confirmed

The results of your MRI and EEG will be looked at by the neurology team at your first-fit clinic appointment. Your GP has also been told about your admission and will be kept in the loop.

---

## Important Advice From Your Doctors

The team has asked you to follow this advice until you have been seen in the neurology clinic:

- **Do not drive.** You must not drive for **6 months from the date of your seizure (19 May).** This is a legal requirement.
- **You must tell the DVLA** that you have had a seizure. It is your responsibility to do this.
- **Do not swim alone.**
- **Do not work at heights.**
- **Do not take a bath on your own** (unsupervised bathing is not safe at this time).

---

## If You Feel Unwell

If you become unwell or are worried about anything, contact your GP or call NHS 111. Call 999 if it is an emergency.

---

*This letter is a draft for review and sign-off by your responsible clinician before it is given to you.*
